review_dimensions.evidence: The closed public request has no authority root, trusted payload, observed digest or verifier outcome. The dependency-injected registry anchor is canonicalized once and its exact identity, version and digest gate the separately observed material.

Each enabled admission reads the material callback once. Canonical plain-data cloning and deep freezing occur before semantic use; the raw authority object is not reused and post-verification mutation cannot change the frozen result.
Externally anchored registry bytes bind producer identity/version, source identity, schema, contract, verifier identity/version, payload digest, trust root and validity interval.

Decision and instrument identity, complete sorted opportunity membership, outcome/evaluator identity and versions, provider lineage and evaluator/outcome lineage are independently reconciled against the immutable P.2A authority snapshot.

Duplicate admission and outcome identities are terminal conflicts. Since one externally anchored Q authority admits one immutable source payload, duplicate source/opportunity observations share the bound outcome identity and are rejected by the batch collision gate.
Canonical integer nanoseconds enforce decision < outcome start <= outcome end <= finalization <= capture <= cutoff and registry validity. P.2A explicit instants must match the Q projection exactly.

Predictor cutoff equals decision time, outcome visibility is false, decision/provider source timestamps are separately bounded and O.2A independently retains split predictor and label digests. Outcome values never enter the Q predictor projection.

Request, material, registry and payload sections carry canonical observed digests, dispositions, expected bindings, verifier versions and sorted reasons. Nested decision/context/outcome changes are transitively bound by the source-payload and immutable P.2A material digests.

Failure identity binds taxonomy, request, observed provenance, expected registry and reasons. A fresh authority read and deterministic admission rebuild rejects self-consistently recalculated status, reason and terminal-digest tampering.
Authority lookup and runtime introspection failures expose only versioned sanitized reason codes and projections; exception messages, stacks and backend details are not emitted.
The single ready synthetic Q handoff reaches P.2A captured and O.2A joined without a special adapter. Predictor and label digests remain distinct.

Disabled and kill-switch paths return frozen precomputed sentinels before request inspection, authority reads, source reads, verification or per-call digest work. No provider, database, writer, persistence, canonical, model-input or live path exists.
All twelve cases and the interop handoff are synthetic. No real source access, capture, join, performance, probability or causal claim occurred.

closed_threat_matrix.threat: Caller injects an expected authority root, trusted payload, safety status or observed digest
Self-consistent registry and payload replacement is presented under the certified external anchor
Observed authority material mutates after the callback returns
Producer, schema, contract or verifier identity drifts
Opportunity membership is incomplete or its digest drifts
Evaluator, outcome or provider lineage is substituted
Outcome starts at decision minus one nanosecond, at the decision boundary or one nanosecond after it
Outcome is pending, future relative to cutoff, rolled back or finalized after capture
Different invalid nested outcome inputs have the same taxonomy and reasons
Status, reasons and digests are tampered and self-consistently recalculated
Duplicate admission, source, opportunity or outcome scope is admitted in one batch
Disabled or kill-switch input attempts request, authority, source or digest work
Timezone or input ordering changes canonical output
Provider, database, persistence, writer, Action 665/666 or live dependency is introduced
Lookup exception exposes message, stack or backend detail
